open_points.subject: runtime settings presence and preprocessing
open_points.text:
Each run setting is a row of the start-up table that only the runtime settings module of SPEC_STANDARD 6.11
reads, into a field of the settings object; that module decides how a value is read. A required setting that
is absent ends the start, and an optional one that is absent takes its default.
open_points.question: What exactly counts as absent, and are empty or whitespace-surrounded environment values preserved, trimmed, rejected, or treated as absent for each setting?
options: Only an unset variable is absent; every set value is used verbatim.
An unset or empty variable is absent; other values are used verbatim.
Trim surrounding whitespace, then treat an empty result as absent.
open_points.default_guess: Only an unset variable is absent; do not trim, and validate every set value exactly.

witness.initial: PORTAL_DELIVERER_PORT is set to the empty string while all required settings are valid.
events: The runtime settings module reads PORTAL_DELIVERER_PORT.
outcomes: The empty value counts as absent, so the service starts on port 8850.
The empty value is present but is not a valid port, so startup ends.
witness.observer: The operator and any caller attempting to connect to port 8850.

open_points.subject: port setting
open_points.text: The port is a whole number from 1 to 65535
open_points.question: Which environment-string spellings are valid ports, and what must startup do when the value is not one of them or is outside the range?
options: Accept only non-empty ASCII decimal digits whose value is 1 through 65535; otherwise end startup.
Accept any integer syntax supported by the settings library, including signs or surrounding whitespace; reject only an out-of-range result.
On an invalid optional value, use the default port 8850.
open_points.default_guess: Accept only ASCII decimal digits representing 1 through 65535 and end startup for every other present value.

witness.initial: All settings are valid and PORTAL_DELIVERER_PORT is set to `+8850`.
events: The settings module converts and validates the port.
outcomes: Startup succeeds because `+8850` is accepted as an integer spelling.
Startup ends because the value is not an ASCII decimal representation.
witness.observer: The operator and callers of the service.

open_points.subject: RuntimeEnvironment setting
open_points.text: | `environment` | `RuntimeEnvironment` | `PORTAL_DELIVERER_ENVIRONMENT` | required: the DEVELOPMENT, TEST or PRODUCTION member of = models.RuntimeEnvironment (values `development`, `test`, `production`) |
open_points.question: Must the environment variable equal one of the three lowercase values exactly, and what must startup do with another spelling or an unknown value?
options: Accept exactly `development`, `test`, or `production`; otherwise end startup.
Accept member names and values case-insensitively.
Let the runtime settings library choose coercion and error behavior.
open_points.default_guess: Accept exactly the three lowercase values and end startup for every other present value.

witness.initial: All settings are valid and PORTAL_DELIVERER_ENVIRONMENT is set to `DEVELOPMENT`.
events: The settings module reads the environment setting.
outcomes: Startup succeeds with the DEVELOPMENT member by matching the member name or ignoring case.
Startup ends because only the lowercase value `development` is accepted.

open_points.subject: timezone setting and photo-time interpretation
open_points.text:
a time zone the time zone database does not know ends the
start
open_points.question: Which time-zone database and version are authoritative for recognizing identifiers and resolving offsets, and may aliases be accepted?
options: Use the host operating system's installed IANA database and accept every identifier it recognizes.
Use a pinned IANA/tzdata release and its identifiers and aliases.
Accept only canonical identifiers from a specified closed list.
open_points.default_guess: Use a pinned IANA tzdata release through the runtime's zone-info implementation and accept the identifiers and aliases in that release.

witness.initial: The configured timezone is an identifier present in one deployed time-zone database release but absent from another.
events: An operator starts two otherwise identical installations with different available time-zone database releases.
outcomes: One installation accepts the setting and interprets local camera times using that database.
The other installation ends startup because its database does not know the identifier.
witness.observer: The operator, and later the owner observing delivered photo dates.

open_points.subject: M07 PublicationMark.marked_at
open_points.question: From what authority is `marked_at` obtained, at what point in the mark operation, and is the stored datetime naive UTC, offset-aware UTC, local time, or another representation?
options: Read the system wall clock and store naive UTC.
Read the system wall clock and store offset-aware UTC.
Receive an instant from the caller and store that representation.
open_points.default_guess: Read an injected system wall clock when the mark is committed and store naive UTC, consistently with the product's other delivered datetimes.

witness.initial: A placement exists without a publication mark, and the host's local timezone is not UTC.
events: The owner's calling flow reports a Portal photo id.
The deliverer creates the publication mark.
outcomes: The record holds the current instant as naive UTC.
The record holds the same wall-clock reading as naive local time or as an offset-aware value.
witness.observer: The calling flow or a later operation reading the mark.

open_points.subject: mark operation clock readings
open_points.text:
The calling flow reports the
`photo_id` right after `photo.publish` answers, and the deliverer creates the mark.
open_points.question: How many clock readings may creation of one publication mark take, and which reading supplies `marked_at` if time advances during the operation?
options: Take exactly one reading for a newly created mark and use it everywhere in that operation.
Take separate readings for the durable record and returned result.
Take a reading at request receipt and another at commit, with the commit reading stored.
open_points.default_guess: Take exactly one clock reading after validation and while holding the project lock, and use it for the durable mark and the answer.

witness.initial: A placement has no mark, and a controllable clock returns T1 and then T2.
events: The caller submits a valid mark request.
The operation validates the request, writes the mark, and constructs its answer while the clock advances from T1 to T2.
outcomes: A single reading makes every representation of `marked_at` equal T1.
Multiple readings allow the stored mark and the operation's result, or two generated records, to carry different instants T1 and T2.
witness.observer: The caller and any later reader of the durable mark.

open_points.subject: time-source invariant and Required tests
open_points.text: - INV-16: every security category has an explicit outcome.
open_points.question: What formal invariant states the source, representation, and per-operation reading count for every instant the product writes or compares, and what Required tests item says exactly how those properties must be demonstrated, including creation and replay of `marked_at`?
options: Add one time invariant covering all written and compared instants, with a controllable-clock test and representation assertions.
Add a dedicated invariant for PublicationMark.marked_at and retain the existing A1/A2 rules as the guarantees for file and camera instants.
Leave time behavior only in normative prose without an invariant or Required tests item.
open_points.default_guess: Add a formal invariant that every fresh product timestamp comes from the decided clock, has its decided UTC representation, and uses exactly one reading per operation; require a controllable-clock test showing mark creation uses that reading and replay preserves it unchanged.
